summary: We developed Interactive Space Archive (Lost Orbit), an interactive educational web application featuring 360° rotatable 3D globes and surface landing maps for the Moon and Mars. The platform addresses the challenge by enabling users to explore historical, decommissioned space equipment via landing-site coordinate markers projected from official NASA and JPL datasets, where clicking a coordinate marker displays 3D rotatable visual media alongside detailed mission field reports. This project is important because it builds space awareness and a scientific mindset among school-aged youth, highlighting retired rovers and landers not as mere space debris, but as historic milestones preserving human ingenuity and key lessons for future space exploration.
details: We developed Interactive Space Archive (Lost Orbit), an educational web application hosted on manus.space that allows users to explore historic Moon and Mars landing sites. The platform features two core exploration modes: a 360-degree rotatable 3D globe and interactive surface maps powered by precise NASA/JPL coordinate datasets. Selecting coordinate markers reveals rotatable 3D visual media from official NASA resources alongside comprehensive mission field reports. The project catalogs decommissioned missions—including Apollo, Surveyor 3, Viking, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity—to build space awareness and a scientific mindset among youth. Rather than viewing retired spacecraft as mere space debris, the platform highlights them as historic milestones preserving human ingenuity and key lessons for future space exploration. Developed under the creative concept "Abandoned but Not Forgotten", it transforms silent space artifacts into an interactive digital learning museum. Ultimately, the system successfully combines educational accessibility with official scientific data, spatial mapping datasets, and rich visual narratives.
